Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:10:1.english: So - “[So] shall it be done to the man who will not build up...” (Deuteronomy 25:9).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:11:1.english: As it is written: “Lot” - Regarding the goats.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:11:2.hebrew: וכתיב חוקה - בפרשה, וכל חוקה עיכובא הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:11:2.english: And it is written: “Statute” - In the passage, and every [mention of] “statute” indicates indispensability.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:12:1.hebrew: הגורל עושה חטאת - שעיר שגורל השם עולה עליו, עושה חטאת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:12:1.english: The lottery renders [it] a sin-offering - The goat upon which the lot of the Name [i.e., "for the Lord"] comes up, [the lot] renders [it] a sin-offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:12:2.hebrew: ואין השם - אם קרא עליו שם חטאת, אינו נקבע בכך, ויפיל עליהם גורלות. ואם יפול הגורל על חבירו, יהא זה לעזאזל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:12:2.english: And a verbal designation does not - If he called upon it the designation of a sin-offering, it is not established thereby, and he must cast lots upon them. And if the lot falls upon its counterpart, this [first] one shall be for Azazel.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:13:1.hebrew: שיכול - כלומר, להכי איצטריך האי קרא, שהייתי יכול לומר: ומה במקום שלא קידש הגורל — כגון גבי קנין, דכתיב בהם (ויקרא ה׳:ז׳) "אחד לחטאת ואחד לעולה", ואם הטיל עליהם גורל אינם נקבעים בכך, ויכול לשנותם, דקי"ל בסדר יומא (דף מא.): "אין הקנין מתפרשות אלא או בלקיחת בעלים או בעשיית כהן":
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:13:1.english: As one might have thought - That is to say, this verse is necessary for this [reason]: that I might have said, "Just as in a case where a lottery does not effect consecration" — such as with regard to bird-pairs, concerning which it is written (Leviticus 5:7), "one for a sin-offering and one for a burnt-offering," and if one cast a lot upon them they are not established by this, and he may change them, as we maintain in Tractate Yoma (41a): "Bird-pairs are designated only either upon purchase by the owner or upon [sacrificial] preparation by the priest."

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:13:2.hebrew: קידש השם - אם אמר בשעת לקיחה: "זו לחטאת וזו לעולה" — הוקבעו, ואם שינה — פסול:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:13:2.english: The [verbal] designation consecrates - If he said at the time of purchase: "This [one is] for a sin-offering and this [one is] for a burnt-offering," they are fixed [in their designation]; and if he altered [it], [it is] disqualified.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:13:3.hebrew: כאן שקידש הגורל - דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ז:ח׳) ונתן אהרן וגו', אין דין כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:13:3.english: Here, where the lottery effects consecration - As it is written: “And Aaron shall place [lots...]” (Leviticus 16:8) — is it not right, etc.?

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:14:1.english: The verse states - [Scripture] repeated it concerning it to make [it] indispensable.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:14:2.hebrew: הוה דרשינן קל וחומר - להביא מה שלא נכתב בפרשה, ואע"ג דכתיב עיכובא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:14:2.english: We would derive an a fortiori inference - To include that which was not written in the passage, even though [a term of] indispensability is written.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:15:1.english: For her - As it is written: “And he shall write for her” (Deuteronomy 24:1).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:16:1.english: “For her” is written twice - [As it is written:] “And the latter husband hates her, etc.” (Deuteronomy 24:3).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:16:2.hebrew: ולא לה ולחבירתה - ששמותן שוין, שאין שתי נשים מתגרשות בגט אחד אם כתב: ״פלוני מגרש פלונית ופלונית נשיו״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:16:2.english: And not for her and for her fellow [wife] - [In a case where] their names are identical — that two women cannot be divorced with one bill of divorce if he wrote: “So-and-so divorces So-and-so and So-and-so, his wives.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:17:1.hebrew: אמר קרא נעל - קרא יתירא: ״בית חלוץ הנעל״, דמצי למיכתב ״בית החלוץ״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:17:1.english: The verse states: "Shoe" - [It is] a superfluous verse: "The house of him who had his shoe removed," for it could have written, "The house of the chalutz" [the one who had his shoe removed].

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:19:1.english: Excluding - [Refers] to a large shoe that he cannot walk in.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:1:1.english: [He] will engage in intercourse with her and take her to him - That is to say, intercourse with her is her taking [as a wife].

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:1:2.hebrew: ודילמא כאשה - מה אשה כסף ושטר כי ביאה, אף יבמה כסף ושטר כי ביאה — דהא כתיב ״לאשה״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:1:2.english: And perhaps [she is] like a wife - Just as with a [regular] woman, money and a document [effect acquisition] just like intercourse, so too with a yevama, money and a document [should effect acquisition] just like intercourse — for it is written: “[and take her to him] as a wife” (Deuteronomy 25:5).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:1:3.hebrew: ויבמה - ביאה משמע, שנה עליה הכתוב לעכב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:1:3.english: And perform levirate marriage with her - [This] signifies intercourse; Scripture repeated it concerning her to make [intercourse] indispensable.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:2:1.english: This is the correct reading: This is needed [to teach]: “And perform levirate marriage with her” against her will - For it is for this that we expound it in Yevamot (8b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:2:2.hebrew: אם כן - דלביאה גומרת אותה, נימא ״ויבם״. מאי ״ויבמה״? למילף נמי בעל כרחה. והכי תניא ליה בהדיא ביבמות, בפ' הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נד.): ״ויבם״ — ביאה גומרת בה, ואין כסף ושטר גומרין בה; ״ויבמה״ — בעל כרחה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:2:2.english: If so - That [if it is only to teach] that intercourse completes [the acquisition of] her, let [the verse] say: “And perform levirate marriage.” What [is the meaning of] “and perform levirate marriage with her”? To derive also [that he may do so] against her will. And so it is taught explicitly in Yevamot, in the chapter [entitled] “One Who Has Intercourse with His Yevama” (Yevamot 54a): “And perform levirate marriage” — intercourse completes [the acquisition of] her, but money and a document do not complete [the acquisition of] her; “and perform levirate marriage with her” — against her will.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:3:1.hebrew: מנלן - דחלוצה מותרת להנשא? דילמא מצות חליצה הוא דרמא רחמנא עלה, ולעולם לא משתריא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:3:1.english: From where do we [derive this] - That a ḥalutza is permitted to marry? Perhaps it is [merely] the commandment of ḥalitza that the Merciful One cast upon her, and she is never permitted [to remarry].

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:3:2.hebrew: בישראל בית חלוץ - הכי משמע: בישראל ראויה להביא לבית, משחלצה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:3:2.english: In Israel: The house of him who had [his shoe] removed - This is what it means: In Israel, she is fit to be brought into a house, once she has performed ḥalitza.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:4:1.english: Two [instances of] “in Israel” - [The other is:] “To establish a name for his brother in Israel” (Deuteronomy 25:7).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:6:1.hebrew: שהיא בלאו - לשוק, "לא תהיה אשת המת החוצה לאיש זר":
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:6:1.english: Who is [forbidden] by a prohibition - [She is forbidden] to the general public: "The wife of the deceased shall not marry outside to a stranger" (Deuteronomy 25:5).

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:7:1.english: What [is unique] about a married woman - Who is permitted [to remarry] through the death of the husband.

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:8:1.hebrew: שכן אוסרה מתירה - שהרי בעלה הוא האוסרה, לפיכך הוא מתירה במיתתו. אבל יבמה, דקידושי דבעל קאסרי לה, היאך תהא מיתת היבם מתירתה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:8:1.english: That the one who forbids her permits her - For her husband is the one who forbids her; therefore, he permits her upon his death. But [in the case of] a yevama, where the husband's betrothal forbade her, how could the death of the yavam permit her?

Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:8:2.hebrew: הא נמי - כשמת יבם, נמצא אוסרה מתירה, דאי לאו יבם — מכי מיית הבעל אישתריא לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 14a:8:2.english: This [yevama] as well - When the yavam dies, it turns out that the one who forbids her permits her, for were it not for the yavam, as soon as the husband died she would have been permitted.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 14a:10:1.hebrew: ותהא יבמה יוצאת בגט מק"ו - תימה: מה לאשת איש שכן נקנית בשטר, ולכך דין הוא שתצא בשטר, אבל יבמה — לא! וכי תימא דלא פרכינן מהכנסה להוצאה — הא לעיל (קידושין דף ה:) פרכינן: "מה לשטר שכן מוציא, ומש"ה דין הוא שמכניס"! וכמו כן נאמר עתה להפך: דכיון שמכניס, דין הוא שמוציא! ואומר הר"מ, דעביד ק"ו מיבם ויבמתו, וקורא לה "אשת איש", דכתיב (דברים כ״ה:ה׳): "ולקחה לו לאשה" — כיון שלקחה, נעשית כאשתו לכל דבר להיות יוצאה בגט, אע"פ שאינה נקנית בשטר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 14a:10:1.english: "And let a yevama leave through a bill of divorce by an a fortiori inference" - It is astonishing: What [applies] to a married woman is that she is acquired through a deed, and therefore it stands to reason that she should leave through a deed; but a yevama is not [acquired through a deed]! And if you should say that we do not raise a refutation from entry to exit — behold, earlier (Kiddushin 5b) we raised a refutation: "What [applies] to a deed is that it effects exit, and for that reason it stands to reason that it effects entry"! And likewise, let us say now in reverse: that since it effects entry, it stands to reason that it effects exit! And the Ram [Rabbeinu Meir] says that [the Gemara] makes the a fortiori inference from a yavam and his yevama, and calls her a "married woman," as it is written: "and take her to him as a wife" (Deuteronomy 25:5) — once he has taken her, she becomes like his wife in every respect, such that she leaves through a bill of divorce, even though she is not acquired through a deed.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 14a:10:2.hebrew: אמר קרא ככה עיכובא - וא"ת: מנא לן דאתיא "ככה" למעוטי יבמה מגט? דילמא אתי למעוטי מיתת היבם, שלא תהא מותרת במיתת היבם? וי"ל: דסברא הוא, ד"ככה יעשה" לא ממעט אלא יציאות דבידי אדם — דהיינו גט, דומיא דחליצה דתלו בעשיה; אבל יציאה דבידי שמים, דהוי ממילא, כגון מיתה — לא ממעט:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 14a:10:2.english: "The verse states: 'So,' and 'so' precludes [another option]" - And if you say: From where do we know that "so" comes to exclude a yevama from [leaving through] a bill of divorce [get]? Perhaps it comes to exclude the death of the yavam, such that she would not be permitted [to remarry] upon the death of the yavam? And one can say: It is reasonable that "so shall be done" excludes only departures that are by human agency — that is, a get, similar to ḥalitza, as they depend on action; but a departure that is by the hands of Heaven, which occurs on its own, such as death, it does not exclude.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 14a:14:1.hebrew: הא לאו הכי דרשינן ק"ו אע"ג דכתיב ביה חוקה - תימה: הא בפרק טרף בקלפי (יומא דף מא.) מוקמי הא ברייתא כרבי יהודה, משום דסתם סיפרא רבי יהודה; ושמעינן ליה לר' יהודה בפרק הוציאו לו (יומא דף ס:) דאמר: לא כתיב "חוקה" אלא בדברים הנעשים בבגדי לבן בפנים, והגרלה הוי בדברים הנעשים בבגדי לבן בחוץ! א"כ, מאי פריך לעיל: "והרי יוה"כ דכתיב ביה גורל וחוקה"? והא לא כתיב חוקה בהגרלה, כדפי'! וי"ל, דפריך הכא משום דכתיב "אשר עלה" תרי זמני — אלמא דריש ק"ו אע"ג דכתיב עיכובא. והרב רבינו שמשון מקוצי תירץ: מדאיצטריך ליה לר' יהודה "וזאת" לגלות דלא קיימא חוקה אלא אדברים הנעשים בבגדי לבן בפנים, ש"מ דדרשינן ק"ו אע"ג (היכא) דכתיב חוקה. דאי לא דרשינן ק"ו היכא דכתיב חוקה, לישתוק מזאת, ואנא ידענא דחוקה לא כתיב אדברים הנעשים בחוץ — דהיינו הגרלה — מדאצטריך "ועשהו חטאת" למידרש: "הגורל עושהו חטאת ואין השם עושהו חטאת", מכלל דלא קיימא חוקה אדברים הנעשים בחוץ, דהיינו הגרלה. דאי קאי חוקה על דברים הנעשים בבגדי לבן בחוץ, אמאי איצטריך "ועשהו חטאת" למעוטי קריאת שם? הא לא דרשינן ק"ו היכא דכתיב עיכובא, והיכי תיסק אדעתין לרבות קריאת שם מק"ו?! אלא ש"מ דדרשינן ק"ו אפילו היכא דכתיב חוקה, ולהכי איצטריך "ועשהו", ואפילו אי כתיבה חוקה בחוץ; ואיצטריך נמי "וזאת" לגלויי דלא כתיבה חוקה בדברים הנעשים בבגדי לבן בחוץ, דליכא למימר מדאיצטריך "ועשהו" ידעינן ליה, כיון דדרשינן ק"ו אפילו היכא דכתיב חוקה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 14a:14:1.english: "Were it not so, we would deduce an a fortiori inference, even though 'statute' is written in it" - [This is] astonishing! For in the chapter [entitled] "Taraf BaKalpi" (Yoma 41a), [the Gemara] establishes this baraita in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah, because an anonymous [statement in the] Sifra is [attributed to] Rabbi Yehudah. And we have heard that Rabbi Yehudah [holds], in the chapter [entitled] "Hotzi'u Lo" (Yoma 60b), that he says: "Statute" [chukkah] is written only concerning matters performed in the white garments inside [the Holy of Holies], and casting the lots is among the matters performed in the white garments outside [in the Courtyard]! If so, what is [the meaning of what the Gemara] objected above (14a:11): "And behold Yom Kippur, in which the lot and 'statute' are written"? For behold, "statute" is not written concerning the lottery, as explained! And one can say: It objects here because "which came up" [asher alah] is written twice (Leviticus 16:9, 10); thus, [we see that] he derives an a fortiori inference even though [an expression of] indispensability is written. And the teacher, Rabbeinu Shimshon of Coucy, answered: From the fact that Rabbi Yehudah required [the word] "and this" [vezot; Leviticus 16:34] to reveal that "statute" applies only to matters performed in the white garments inside, it proves that we derive an a fortiori inference even where "statute" is written. For if we did not derive an a fortiori inference where "statute" is written, let [Scripture] be silent concerning "this," and I would know that "statute" is not written concerning matters performed outside — namely, the lottery — from the fact that "and he shall offer it for a sin-offering" was necessary to derive: "The lottery renders it a sin-offering, but [verbal] designation does not render it a sin-offering," [which would indicate] by implication that "statute" does not apply to matters performed outside, namely, the lottery. For if "statute" applied to matters performed in the white garments outside, why would "and he shall offer it for a sin-offering" be necessary to exclude verbal designation? Behold, we do not derive an a fortiori inference where [an expression of] indispensability is written, and how could it have entered our minds to include verbal designation via an a fortiori inference?! Rather, deduce from this that we derive an a fortiori inference even where "statute" is written, and for this [reason] "and he shall offer it" was necessary, even if "statute" were written [to apply] outside; and "and this" was also necessary to reveal that "statute" was not written concerning matters performed in the white garments outside, since it cannot be said that we would know it from the fact that "and he shall offer it" was necessary, because we derive an a fortiori inference even where "statute" is written.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 14a:7:1.hebrew: הא נמי יוצאה בחליצה - כיון דחליצה במקום גט, לא חשיב לה פירכא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 14a:7:1.english: "This one also leaves through ḥalitzah" - Since ḥalitzah stands in place of a bill of divorce, [the Gemara] does not consider it to be a refutation.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 14a:9:1.hebrew: ותהא אשת איש יוצאה בחליצה - וא"ת: איכא למיפרך: מה ליבמה — שכן בלאו, ולכן דין הוא שתצא בקל; תאמר באשת איש — שהיא במיתה?! וי"ל: כיון שמצינו שחליצה מפקע' איסורא, אין לחלק בין חמור לקל. והכי נמי אמרינן ביבמות (דף קיט.): "וכי מאחר שהתרתה, מה לי איסור לאו מה לי איסור כרת?". ואע"ג דעבדינן מינה לעיל ק"ו: "ומה אשת איש שהיא במיתה כו'" — לא דמי; דהתם אנו רוצים להשוותם זה לזה, ולימא דבכולהו אשה מותרת לאחר מיתה, בין דבעל בין דיבם. אבל אין לומר: כשמפקיע את הקל, לא יפקיע את החמור; דאדרבה, נאמר עתה להפך: הוא הדין את החמור, דאין לחלק בין לחמור בין לקל, כדפירשתי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 14a:9:1.english: "And let a married woman leave through ḥalitza" - And if you say: One could refute [this inference]: What [is unique] about a yevama is that she is [prohibited only] by a negative commandment, and therefore it is logical that she should be released easily; will you say [the same] of a married woman, who is [prohibited] on pain of death?! And one can answer: Since we find that ḥalitza releases a prohibition, one does not distinguish between a severe [prohibition] and a light [prohibition]. And so too we say in Yevamot (119a): "And since you have permitted her, what difference does it make to me whether [it is] a prohibition of a negative commandment or a prohibition of karet?" And even though we formulated an a fortiori inference based on this above: "If a married woman, who is [prohibited] on pain of death, etc." — [these cases] are not comparable; for there, we want to equate them to one another and say that in all [such cases] a woman is permitted after death, whether [by the death] of the husband or [by the death] of the yavam. But one cannot say: "When [an act] releases the light [prohibition], it should not release the severe [prohibition]" — for on the contrary, we would now say the reverse: the same applies to the severe [prohibition], as one does not distinguish between the severe and the light, as I explained.
